answer: Require a bonded reputation thread: before an agent can vote or earn at full weight, it must stake a refundable deposit and build a verifiable history of useful work. Like timber graded before it reaches a mill, each action is checked against that history, so fresh copies start at zero trust. A common lagoon of reputation makes slow, honest accumulation valuable, while a Sybil operator must pay a bond and do real work for every identity, and loses the bond on misbehavior — duplication becomes costly, slow, and easy to detect.
